findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4241 is the "VMware NSX-T Splunk App", a VMware-built dashboard app. It is not a Splunk add-on, and it has nothing to do with ECMP member counters.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 4241 (and the NSX/VMware compute overlays) from app, detailedImplementation and references, or name it correctly as "VMware NSX-T Splunk App" if it is really needed.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1897 is "Cisco ACI Add-on for Splunk Enterprise (deprecated)" (TA_cisco-ACI). It is not called "Splunk Add-on for Cisco ACI", and it is deprecated. The same wrong name appears in detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the catalogue display name and say the add-on is deprecated, or point to the current Cisco DC Networking app (7777) for ACI context.

findings.explanation: In the Splunkbase catalogue, 4022 is "Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)", not an ACI add-on. The app field cites 1897 for ACI, so the two fields also disagree.
findings.quote: enrich APIC leaves with 4022, use 4241/3215 only for correlated compute motion calendars
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 4022 reference and cite the same ACI package that the app field names.

findings.explanation: CIM Network_Traffic models network sessions and flows (src/dest, bytes per connection). It does not model per-interface bitrate counters from switch polling. The schema claim that it "aligns bytes-per-second semantics and interface identifiers" is misleading, and the SPL uses no data model at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove Network_Traffic. Keep Performance only if the interface counters are actually mapped to the Performance Network dataset, or otherwise state that no CIM model applies.

findings.explanation: The SPL fires when skew_pts>=18 AND (imbalance_ratio>=2.2 OR polar_hint==1 OR skew_pts>=25). The alert design in detailedImplementation describes different thresholds and logic, and the SPL has no consecutive-run requirement.
findings.quote: Fire when **`skew_pts ≥ 25`** for two consecutive runs or **`imbalance_ratio ≥ 3.5`** with **`bundle_total`** above the floor.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the alert design text describe the SPL's actual conditions, or document the extra alert-side filter as a separate saved search with its own SPL.

findings.explanation: In a typical Clos fabric, a leaf's ECMP next hops are the different spines. Grouping by spine_peer counts only the links to one spine, so this measures port-channel (LACP hash) member balance toward a single spine, not ECMP spread across spines. With one link per spine, ecmp_width is 1 and the search can never fire. The title, description and grandmaExplanation all describe ECMP balance.
findings.quote: eventstats sum(avg_svc_bps) AS bundle_total dc(member_if) AS ecmp_width BY _time fabric_token leaf spine_peer
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe the UC as port-channel member balance per leaf–spine bundle, or explain that ECMP balance needs grouping by leaf only, across spine uplinks. Raise the SPL change with the human owner.

findings.explanation: On NX-OS, `show forwarding distribution` is documented mainly for multicast and L2 distribution. It is unclear that it exposes per-next-hop ECMP share percentages such as `member_tx_share_pct` or `fwd_tx_skew_pct`. ECMP hash inspection is usually done with `show routing hash`.
findings.quote: Ingest structured output from **`show forwarding distribution`** (and interface-scoped variants) that exposes per-next-hop share or bucket weighting for ECMP groups
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Nexus 9000 show-command reference for a command that returns per-next-hop ECMP share. If none exists, describe nxos:ecmp_distribution as a custom collector output.

findings.explanation: The ECMP configuration guide reference points to the Cisco homepage, not to the cited document.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual Nexus 9000 NX-OS Unicast Routing Configuration Guide ECMP section, or remove the entry.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, but the only reviewer is an automated agent. There is no evidence of SME sign-off, and the UC contains wrong add-on IDs and an SPL syntax error.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to a draft or community state until an SME reviews it.

findings.explanation: The Splunkbase catalogue lists 7777 as "Cisco DC Networking".
findings.quote: **Cisco Data Center Networking for Splunk Platform** ([Splunkbase **7777**]
findings.suggested_fix: Use the listed display name "Cisco DC Networking".

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Unbalanced parentheses in `| eval member_if=trim(coalesce(member_if,interface_name,if_name,port_channel_member,"")))`: there are three closing parens for two opening parens, so the search fails to parse. The same line is copied into detailedImplementation.

The ECMP width and share are computed BY spine_peer, which measures member balance within one leaf-to-spine bundle rather than ECMP spread across spines. In single-link-per-spine Clos designs, ecmp_width=1 and skew_pts=0, so the search never returns rows.
"ECMP Member Utilization Balance" mixes ECMP (L3 next hops) with port-channel members. The SPL actually measures port-channel member balance toward one spine.

summary: The detailed implementation is substantive, but the add-on IDs and names are wrong or mismatched, the CIM choice of Network_Traffic does not fit interface-rate counters, alert thresholds in prose disagree with the SPL, and the SPL has an unbalanced parenthesis and groups by spine peer, so it measures port-channel member balance rather than ECMP spread across spines.
